thread:
Maya: quick thread 1 - need to finalize concessions for dedicated capacity launch checklist. Main tradeoffs: carryover generosity vs. utilization, and preempt policy strictness vs. enterprise SLAs. Thoughts?
Arjun: technical: larger carryover increases idle reserved capacity exposure. Implementation cheap (ledger entry) but allocator complexity rises if carryover tokens are redeemable into instant slots. Recommend hard cap and TTL.
Sienna: ops: preemption softness matters. If we allow aggressive reclaim during spikes, we see a spike in 5xx errors. Suggest default drain=60s and evictions logged per-tenant. Also require an ops alert when evictions > 0.5% for 10m.
Leo: customers pushing for predictability. A fintech pilot asked for a "no-preempt" window during business hours and contract clause. They're willing to pay. Need plan to support 2 pilots at launch.
Priya: sales: pricing needs to be simple. Propose bundle: reserved pool + 200 instant tokens/month + carryover up to 15% by default. Shield add-on for business-hours non-preemptible window.
Dan: finance: keep carryover simple to account for. Credits that convert to lower-rate bursts are okay, but cannot be sold between tenants. We need invoice lines that clearly separate reserved usage, burst usage, carryover consumption, and shield premiums.
Maya: draft compromise: carryover cap 15% of monthly instant tokens, TTL 72h; preempt policy: opportunistic label for cheap bursts, drain_seconds=60, eviction audit log. Business-hours shield = paid add-on, manual opt-in for pilots. Launch gates: RFC, console counters, eviction metrics, billing export, 2 pilot customers.
Arjun: config sketch: 
```
burst_policy:
  carryover_percent: 15
  carryover_ttl_hours: 72
  drain_seconds: 60
  opportunistic_label: true
  shield_feature_flag: pilot_only
```
Arjun: note: kernel reclaim might require bumping drain to 75s on some hardware. We'll test on canary fleets.
Sienna: monitoring: tenant.evictions.count, tenant.evictions.rate5m, tenant.drain.latency.p50/p95, cluster.instant.utilization. Alerts: evictions_rate > 0.5% for 10m -> page oncall.
Leo: will coordinate with the fintech pilot; can confirm willingness to buy shield add-on. Also request explicit exportable eviction audit for contract compliance.
Priya: will prepare sales one-pager and pricing table. Dan: can you draft invoice template lines?
Dan: yes - will do and coordinate with revenue ops. Need final carryover rules to finish.
rfc-bot: RFC up: https://redwood.infra/rfc/dedicated-launch-concessions-2026 - comments due Friday.
Maya: timeline: week0 RFC -> week1 impl ledger + console counters -> week2 allocator/drain test on canary -> week3 pilot enablement -> week4 limited beta. Owners: Arjun (impl), Sienna (ops), Leo (pilot), Priya (sales), Dan (billing), Maya (PM).
Sienna: rollback plan: disable carryover and opportunistic routing; revert to single reserved pool if evictions or latency regress > threshold for 15m.
Arjun: will add circuit-breaker to allocator to pause opportunistic pools if cluster errors spike.
Maya: thanks everyone, I'll update the RFC with these concessions and the launch checklist. Sync tomorrow 10am PT to sign off. End.
